\documentclass{article}
% SYNTHETIC test fixture (CONTRACT §"Shell escape per paper", Security). multibib's \newcites names an auxiliary .aux
% file that reaches latexmk's bibtex command line only after TeX has run. Were the name run through /bin/sh, the
% backquote would run `date>MARK` and leave a file MARK in the build. The engine runs bibtex as an argv list, so none
% appears. The \csname … \endcsname forms spell multibib's generated \citex…x, \bibliographystylex…x and \bibliographyx…x.
\usepackage{multibib}
\newcites{x`date>MARK`x}{More References}
\begin{document}
Kelp drifts \csname citex`date>MARK`x\endcsname{kelp} across the page here.
\csname bibliographystylex`date>MARK`x\endcsname{plain}
\csname bibliographyx`date>MARK`x\endcsname{refs}
\end{document}
